title: Bongo Cat
genre: Desktop companion / idle clicker ('desktop pet' overlay) with Steam item drops and cosmetics
release_date: 2025-03-05 (Steam: Windows/macOS/Linux) [CONFIRMED – Steam store page / SteamDB]. Note: the brief said ~May–June 2025; that was the peak virality period (all-time CCU peak in May 2025), not the launch.
early_access_date: n/a (free demo app on Steam from ~early Feb 2025, featured in the Steam Idler Fest before launch [ESTIMATE – Game*Spark 2025-02-07, meme wiki pages])
window_note: Edge of window: launched 2025-03-05 (about one month before the April 2025 window), but its viral peak (193,859 CCU, May 2025), the press wave (May–June 2025), the 188.8k CCU resurgence (Sep 2026) and its continued top-100 status through Oct 2026 all fall inside the window. Included as a benchmark for an ultra-cheap viral desktop-companion F2P.
developer: Marcel Zurawka and Julius Krüger (credited developers), Irox Games
team_size: 2 credited developers (Marcel Zurawka, Julius Krüger) [CONFIRMED – Steam/SteamDB credits, GameGrin, GamesMarkt]. Irox Games was founded in 2020 by two friends [CONFIRMED – WinFuture]; total studio headcount not disclosed.
developer_background: Irox Games is a small Bavarian studio founded in 2020 by two friends. Before Bongo Cat it was working on 'Oku' (a watercolour, Japan-inspired 3D exploration adventure) and pitching publishers ('before, we knocked on 50 doors; now, they are coming to us' – CEO Marcel Zurawka via PC Gamer/Eurogamer). Bongo Cat was built as an experiment with the Steam Community Market and became the studio's marketing engine. Irox now also publishes other games (Nightwater, an island automation game targeted for Q3 2026; Tap Tap Loot by Turtle Knight Games, billed as Bongo Cat's spiritual successor).
platforms_and_store_links: Steam (Windows/macOS/Linux): https://store.steampowered.com/app/3419430/Bongo_Cat/ ; Demo app: https://steamcharts.com/app/3487310 ; Paid cosmetic DLC e.g. God Pack: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3929900/Bongo_Cat__God_Pack/
business_model: Free-to-play. Revenue from (1) paid cosmetic skins/DLC packs (main source per the CEO; 2026 packs such as Mecha Pack ~$5 and God/Wrestler/Squirrel/Wild Wonders packs ~$10 [ESTIMATE – DekuDeals/Steam price snapshots]) and (2) the publisher fee on Steam Community Market trades of the random hat/skin/emote drops (one chest every 30 min of runtime, opened with 1,000 taps). Market fees were 'generally less than half' of total income [CONFIRMED – Zurawka via Eurogamer, reported by GameSpot/PC Gamer]. It also serves as a cross-promotion tool: items are granted for wishlisting Oku/Nightwater or playing demos.
price_usd: Free (paid cosmetic DLC ~$5–$10 per pack in 2026 [ESTIMATE – DekuDeals/Steam snapshots])
units_or_downloads: 5.7 million total players, 'almost 6 million', after crossing 5 million in Jan 2026 [CONFIRMED – Irox Games figures via GamesMarkt, ~Mar 2026]. Third-party: VG Insights 5.2–5.4M 'units' [ESTIMATE – VGI via SteamPulse]; Raijin 2.82M units / ~265k–297k 'owners' [ESTIMATE – Raijin, low reliability for F2P]. Note: the CEO estimated ~50% of concurrent players are bots farming market drops, so real human players are lower.
peak_concurrent_players: 193,859 all-time peak, May 2025 [ESTIMATE – SteamCharts tracker; Steambase lists 194,508 on 2025-05-04]. Re-approached the record with 188,817 in Sep 2026 (SteamCharts) and 187,909 on 2026-07-15 (SteamDB). 24h peaks ~179k in late Sep/early Oct 2026 [ESTIMATE – SteamDB/GameDropDaily]. Launch-week peak ~134k (Mar 2025, press). CEO estimated ~50% of the ~170k concurrents were bots [CONFIRMED – Zurawka via Eurogamer/PC Gamer, June 2025].
steam_reviews: 108,446 reviews, 97% positive ('Overwhelmingly Positive'), ~Sep/Oct 2026 [ESTIMATE – SteamPulse tracker]; 91,000+ reviews, 97% positive ~Mar 2026 [GamesMarkt citing Steam].
implied_review_multiplier: ~63 players per review (5.7M players ÷ ~91k reviews, both ~Mar 2026) [ESTIMATE]. This is a free-to-play player ratio (including bot accounts), not a purchase ratio; it is not comparable to premium Boxleiter multipliers.
gross_revenue: Reported net figures: $2,000 (Mar 2025, net after Steam cut), $4,050 (Apr), $3,800 (May), $2,800 (June, partial) = $12,650 net in ~3.5 months; ~$3,000/month on average [CONFIRMED – Zurawka via Eurogamer, reported by PC Gamer/GameSpot, late June 2025]. Implied gross for the first 3.5 months ≈ $12,650 ÷ (0.70 × 0.93) ≈ $19,000–$20,000 [ESTIMATE]. Lifetime gross to Oct 2026: ≈ $70,000–$150,000 [ESTIMATE – 19 months at the ~$4.5k/month implied gross run-rate, with upside from the ~$5–$10 cosmetic packs launched Apr–Jun 2026; low confidence, no 2026 figures disclosed].
net_revenue: ≈ $3,000/month net in 2025 [CONFIRMED – CEO]. Lifetime net to Oct 2026 ≈ $45,000–$100,000 [ESTIMATE – run-rate extrapolation; Steam 30% cut on DLC, and on market trades the developer only receives its game-fee share (~10% of each sale; Steam keeps 5%)]. The CEO said that on the numbers alone it was 'actually losing us money' because it did not cover even one developer salary.
production_cost: No disclosed figure. ≈ $25,000–$40,000 to launch [ESTIMATE – 2 devs × ~2–3 months × ~$6k/month (Germany lean indie)], plus ongoing live-ops (new skins, co-op 'Meowtiplayer' rooms, UI themes, events, anti-bot work) that the CEO said the revenue did not cover in 2025.
development_time: Demo on Steam by ~early Feb 2025 (Game*Spark, 2025-02-07); full launch 2025-03-05 [CONFIRMED – Steam]. Total build time not disclosed; likely weeks to a few months for the core app [ESTIMATE]. Continuous updates since launch (multiplayer rooms Aug 2025, paid packs 2026).
why_popular: (1) Instantly recognisable 2018 meme: a white blob-like cat slapping a table, posted by @StrayRogue on 2018-05-07; @DitzyFlama's reply added bongos and Super Mario World music, and the format spread to countless songs. A fan-made 'bongocat' key-mapping overlay already existed for osu! streamers. (2) Zero-friction: free, ~100 MB, sits on the taskbar and drums along to your typing/clicking, so it's 'played' while you work or game. (3) Collectible loot: a random hat/skin chest every 30 min, with rarity tiers down to 1-in-500,000 legendaries, all tradable on the Steam Community Market for wallet money, which drives long idle sessions (and bots). (4) Steam's charts amplified it: top-5/top-10 most-played lists produced 'what is this game?' press and social posts. (5) Achievements and a tap counter give light progression.
marketing_channels: Meme nostalgia and recognisability; Steam demo + Idler Fest + March 2025 Next Fest exposure; Steam most-played charts (a self-reinforcing loop driven by idling); press curiosity pieces (GameSpot, Insider Gaming, PC Gamer, GamesRadar, Automaton, WinFuture, RTBF); Reddit/TikTok/YouTube desktop-setup clips; market-trading communities. Later used to cross-promote Irox's own and published games (items for wishlisting Oku/Nightwater).
engine: Unity (Unity 6) [ESTIMATE – Irox publishing page/third-party listing; Unity rebuild noted by meme wiki pages]
art_style: Minimal 2D cartoon: a flat white blob-cat with simple line art, overlaid on the desktop taskbar; many cosmetic hats, skins and emotes
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write nearly all the code (transparent always-on-top overlay window, global keyboard/mouse hook counter, Steamworks inventory service item drops/item definitions, achievements, simple lobby rooms); generate the 2D sprite and hundreds of cosmetic variants (hats, skins, emotes); produce SFX (bongo hits) and UI. | AI cannot: supply a famous meme IP (Bongo Cat rode a 2018 meme of disputed licensing; StrayRogue's terms ask for credit, and Game*Spark questioned whether permission was granted); tune the drop economy and fight market bots; create the viral moment/Steam-chart loop; handle community management and live-ops cadence. Steam Inventory Service setup and Market eligibility also take time and Valve review. | Toolset: Claude Code + Unity 6 or Godot 4 (GodotSteam) + Steamworks Inventory Service; Retro Diffusion/Scenario/Midjourney for 2D cosmetics; ElevenLabs SFX; native OS hooks (Win32/macOS accessibility APIs) for global input.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 2–4 weeks, $150–$400 (Claude Pro/Max 1 month $20–$200, image gen $10–$30, Steam Direct $100). Excludes the developer's own living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 2–4 months, $1,000–$4,000 (subscriptions for 3–4 months, freelance character art/animation polish for an original mascot $500–$2,000, cosmetic sets, macOS signing/notarisation $99/yr, small marketing/playtest budget). Excludes living costs. Note: the revenue upside of this model is small (Bongo Cat earned ~$3k/month net at ~170k CCU); its value is as a funnel or marketing tool.

data_conflicts: Release date: the brief said ~May–June 2025; Steam/SteamDB say 2025-03-05 (May–June 2025 was the viral/press peak). All-time CCU peak: 193,859 (SteamCharts, May 2025) vs 194,508 on 2025-05-04 (Steambase); I used ~194k. SteamDB's own recorded peak (187,909 on 2026-07-15) only covers its data since July 2026. Player counts: Irox's 5.7M total players (CONFIRMED, ~Mar 2026) vs VG Insights 5.2–5.4M 'units' vs Raijin 2.82M units / ~265k–297k 'owners'. Raijin's owner model is unreliable for F2P, so I used the official figure. Bots: the CEO estimates ~50% of concurrents are bots, so CCU overstates real human play. Engine: Unity 6 per a third-party listing, not confirmed by the developer. Developer credit: some listings name only Krüger or only Zurawka; Steam/SteamDB list both.
notes: Key lesson for a solo creator: massive CCU does not mean revenue. ~170k concurrents earned only ~$3k/month net in 2025 because the drops are free and the publisher fee on market trades is small. Its real value was as a marketing funnel: Irox went from pitching 50 publishers to being approached, and it now pushes wishlists for its other games via item rewards. The desktop-companion/idle-overlay niche (Bongo Cat, Rusty's Retirement, Cast n Chill, Tap Tap Loot, Desktop Mate) is very AI-friendly and cheap to build, but monetising it needs paid cosmetics or a premium price. Avoid unlicensed meme IP: StrayRogue's terms require credit, and Bongo Cat's licensing was publicly questioned. Related lead: Tap Tap Loot (Turtle Knight Games, published by Irox), a Bongo Cat-style idle typing game, also charted high on Steam (GamesMarkt: 'Two German Typing Games Conquered Steam').
